Outcome_variable.evidence_source: [/page/13/Text/7] This research investigated how the palliative effect of system justification functions in the short and longer-term. Results from a large cross-sectional nationally representative sample (Study 1), and a longitudinal sample of undergraduates (Study 2) indicated that system justification acts as a buffer against the negative effects of generalized and abstracted experiences of active harm on life satisfaction in the short-term. [/page/14/Text/2] showed that the buffering effect of system justification does not hold longer-term. People who experienced more active harm and who were higher in system justification at Time 1 had lower life satisfaction the following year
